$comment: Generated by tools/contracts/build.ts from packages/contracts/tools; do not edit. A null scope means any valid personal token may call the tool.
instructions: Kinship is a personal relationship manager: people and their profiles, relationships, notes and activities, tasks, reminders, a journal, and gifts and debts, in one workspace. Only the tools this token's scopes allow are listed, and the member's role can still refuse a call. Call get_context first to see the workspace, role, and scopes. Find a person's id with list_people or search_workspace before reading or writing about them. Read before you update: updates and deletes take expectedUpdatedAt or another revision from the matching list or get tool, and a stale one is refused as a conflict, so read again. On creates that take a requestId, pass your own UUID and reuse it when you retry; after what it made is deleted that requestId is refused, so use a new one. A refused call returns isError with the problem code and field messages; correct the arguments rather than retrying unchanged.

tools.name: get_context
tools.title: Get the token's context
tools.description: Reads what this connection acts as: the token's name, scopes, and expiry, and the workspace, member, and current role it uses. Call it first to learn which kinds of change the scopes allow; the member's role can still refuse a change the scopes allow.

tools.name: search_workspace
tools.title: Search the workspace
tools.description: Searches the workspace's people, notes, activities, journal posts, and tasks for q, answering each group separately with at most limit results (default 5, at most 10): people with their ids and names, and each note, activity, journal post, or task with its id, its person, and a short snippet of what matched. People are answered first; a text group that cannot be searched is marked unavailable while the others still answer. A blank q answers the member's recently viewed people and leaves every other group empty. Use list_people to page through people.

tools.name: get_today_attention
tools.title: Get what needs attention today
tools.description: Reads what needs attention, in the member's time zone: overdue, today, and next-seven-days groups and an upcoming list of open tasks, undelivered or failing reminders, important dates, life events, and stay-in-touch cadences that are due, each with its person. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone.

tools.name: get_today_reminders
tools.title: Get upcoming reminders
tools.description: Reads reminder occurrences that are due within thirty days, being retried, failed, or need attention, the recently sent ones, and stay-in-touch cadences due within thirty days, each with its person. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone.

tools.name: get_today_tasks
tools.title: Get upcoming tasks
tools.description: Reads up to twenty open tasks due within thirty days, overdue ones included, earliest first, each with its linked person. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone. Use list_tasks for every task.

tools.name: get_today_favorite_notes
tools.title: Get favourite notes
tools.description: Reads the workspace's favourite notes — notes recorded or marked with isFavorited — with their full bodies and the people they are about. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone.

tools.name: get_today_recent_activity
tools.title: Get recent notes and activities
tools.description: Reads up to twenty of the workspace's most recent notes and activities, with their content and participants. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone.

tools.name: get_today_recent_people
tools.title: Get recently viewed people
tools.description: Reads the people the token's member most recently opened in the web app, newest first, with their ids, names, and whether they are archived. Tool calls do not count as views. It is a read-only Today projection across people, readable with today:read alone.

tools.name: list_people
tools.title: List people
tools.description: Searches and pages through the people in the token's workspace and returns each one's id, names, star, lifecycle, and up to five tags. Call it first to find a person's id: search matches names; tag filters by a tag id from list_tags; starred and starredFirst use the workspace star; archived people need lifecycle "archived". Returns at most limit people (default 20, at most 50) and a nextCursor to pass back with the same filters for the next page. It reads the directory only, not profiles.

starredFirst.description: Starred people before everybody else, each group in the sort order.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: Lists the workspace's tags with their ids, twenty at a time: search filters by name, nextCursor pages, and selected resolves one tag id you already hold. Use a tag id to filter list_people, with add_tag_to_people, or in update_person_tags. New tags are made with create_tag.

tools.name: list_tag_counts
tools.title: Count people per tag
tools.description: Counts how many active people carry each tag (archived people with lifecycle "archived"), most carried first, at most thirty tags with their ids and names; truncated says more tags are in use.

tools.name: get_person
tools.title: Get a person's name
tools.description: Reads one person's id, names (given, middle, family, nickname, and whether the record is partial), whether they are archived, and updatedAt, their current revision: pass it as expectedUpdatedAt to update_person, archive_person, or restore_person. It returns no profile, notes, or timeline: use list_profile_facts, list_important_dates, list_relationships, and the other area tools for those. Use it to confirm which person an id names before writing about them.

tools.name: create_person
tools.title: Create a person
tools.description: Creates a person from their names and returns the new person's id and updatedAt, the revision update_person, archive_person, and restore_person need. isPartial marks an incomplete record; send false for an ordinary person. A person whose name matches someone already in the workspace is refused as a possible duplicate (409): check list_people first, and resend with duplicateOverride true only when it really is someone else, with the same requestId. Pass your own requestId and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and names return the person it created, at their current revision, while different names under it, or a retry after that person was deleted, are refused as a conflict (person_request_conflict).

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: update_person
tools.title: Update a person
tools.description: Replaces a person's names, and optionally their description, gender, and deceased flag. The names are replaced whole, so send every name to keep; description, genderOptionId, and isDeceased are kept when left out, and an empty string clears the description or the gender. genderOptionId comes from list_vocabulary_entries (section gender-options), which requires vocabularies:read and an owner or admin; a token or member without them cannot obtain one. expectedUpdatedAt is the person's current revision: person.updatedAt from get_person, from create_person, or from the last update_person, archive_person, or restore_person answer. get_person requires people:profile:read; without it, a token has only the revisions create_person and those answers return. A stale revision is refused as a conflict: read it again with get_person. An archived person cannot be edited until restore_person.

tools.name: archive_person
tools.title: Archive a person
tools.description: Archives a person: they leave the active directory and their profile becomes read-only until restore_person. Nothing is deleted. expectedUpdatedAt is the person's current revision: person.updatedAt from get_person, from create_person, or from the last update_person, archive_person, or restore_person answer. get_person requires people:profile:read; without it, a token has only the revisions create_person and those answers return. A stale revision is refused as a conflict: read it again with get_person.

tools.name: restore_person
tools.title: Restore an archived person
tools.description: Returns an archived person to the active directory and makes their profile writable again. expectedUpdatedAt is the person's current revision: person.updatedAt from get_person, from create_person, or from the last update_person, archive_person, or restore_person answer. get_person requires people:profile:read; without it, a token has only the revisions create_person and those answers return. A stale revision is refused as a conflict: read it again with get_person.

tools.name: add_person_star
tools.title: Star a person
tools.description: Stars a person for the whole workspace, not only for this member, so list_people can filter on starred or put starred people first. Safe to repeat: starring a starred person changes nothing. An archived person's star cannot change.

tools.name: remove_person_star
tools.title: Unstar a person
tools.description: Removes a person's workspace star. Safe to repeat: an unstarred person is unchanged. An archived person's star cannot change.

tools.name: archive_people
tools.title: Archive several people
tools.description: Archives several people at once, as archive_person does for one; restore them with restore_people. Names 1 to 100 distinct people (personIds from list_people). Each person is changed on their own and answered in request order as done, unchanged, skipped, or failed with a code, so one refusal does not undo the others; only a malformed request or lost access refuses them all. No revision is needed.

personIds.description: Distinct people in the active workspace.

tools.name: restore_people
tools.title: Restore several people
tools.description: Restores several archived people at once, as restore_person does for one. Names 1 to 100 distinct people (personIds from list_people). Each person is changed on their own and answered in request order as done, unchanged, skipped, or failed with a code, so one refusal does not undo the others; only a malformed request or lost access refuses them all. No revision is needed.

personIds.description: Distinct people in the active workspace.

tools.name: add_tag_to_people
tools.title: Tag several people
tools.description: Adds one tag (tagId, required, from list_tags) to several people, keeping their other tags. Names 1 to 100 distinct people (personIds from list_people). Each person is changed on their own and answered in request order as done, unchanged, skipped, or failed with a code, so one refusal does not undo the others; only a malformed request or lost access refuses them all. No revision is needed. A tag outside the workspace refuses the whole request.

personIds.description: Distinct people in the active workspace.

tagId.description: The workspace tag to add or remove; only tagging names one.

tools.name: remove_tag_from_people
tools.title: Untag several people
tools.description: Removes one tag (tagId, required, from list_tags) from several people, keeping their other tags; the tag itself stays in the workspace. Names 1 to 100 distinct people (personIds from list_people). Each person is changed on their own and answered in request order as done, unchanged, skipped, or failed with a code, so one refusal does not undo the others; only a malformed request or lost access refuses them all. No revision is needed.

personIds.description: Distinct people in the active workspace.

tagId.description: The workspace tag to add or remove; only tagging names one.

tools.name: get_person_deletion_impact
tools.title: Preview deleting a person
tools.description: Reads what deleting a person means and the exact confirmation phrase delete_person must repeat, with the person's identity and current updatedAt. Call it immediately before delete_person, and when acting for a user, show them the phrase and get their agreement first.

tools.name: delete_person
tools.title: Delete a person
tools.description: Deletes a person from the workspace. Send confirmation exactly as get_person_deletion_impact returned it and expectedUpdatedAt as that read's person.updatedAt; a changed phrase or revision is refused. It is a soft delete that no tool can undo: the person leaves every list and restore_person cannot bring them back, while the records that mention them are retained. Prefer archive_person to keep someone out of the way.

tools.name: list_duplicate_people
tools.title: List possible duplicates
tools.description: Lists up to twenty pairs of active people who look like the same person — the same full name, email address, or phone number — with both people's ids, names, and updatedAt and the reasons; truncated says there are more. Follow with get_merge_preview for a pair to merge, or set_not_duplicates for a pair that is two people.

tools.name: set_not_duplicates
tools.title: Dismiss a possible duplicate
tools.description: Marks two people (personIds, in any order) as not the same person for the whole workspace, so list_duplicate_people stops offering the pair to every member. Safe to repeat.

tools.name: get_merge_preview
tools.title: Preview a merge
tools.description: Previews merging duplicateId into primaryId, the person who is kept: the single-valued facts that conflict and which value is kept or discarded, how many records move, both people's current identities and updatedAt, and the conflictsDigest. merge_people must quote that digest and both revisions.

tools.name: merge_people
tools.title: Merge two people
tools.description: Merges duplicateId into primaryId: every record of the duplicate moves to the primary, the values the preview listed as discarded are lost, and the duplicate is deleted. A merge has no undo. Send confirmed true, conflictsDigest from get_merge_preview, primaryRevision and duplicateRevision as that preview's primary.updatedAt and duplicate.updatedAt; if either person changed since, it is refused, so preview again. When acting for a user, confirm with them first.

tools.name: list_important_dates
tools.title: List a person's important dates
tools.description: Lists a person's important dates — birthday, deceased date, first-met date, and custom dates — archived people included, each with its id, updatedAt, and the precision it was stored with: a date may lack its year, month, or day. scheduling says whether it can drive a yearly reminder. Use the id and updatedAt with update_important_date and delete_important_date.

tools.name: add_important_date
tools.title: Add an important date
tools.description: Adds an important date to a person and returns it with its id. precision says which of year, month, and day the date has — full (all three), year_month, month_day, year, month, day, or unknown (none) — and exactly those must be sent. A person has at most one birthday, one deceased date, and one first-met date; any other date is kind custom and needs a label, which the other kinds must not have. isYearApproximate marks a guessed year and isAgeBased shows the date as an age; both need a year. There is no retry key: repeating a custom date adds a second one. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: update_important_date
tools.title: Update an important date
tools.description: Replaces an important date with the value sent (fields left out are cleared). dateId and expectedUpdatedAt are the date's id and updatedAt from list_important_dates; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. That read requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. precision says which of year, month, and day the date has — full (all three), year_month, month_day, year, month, day, or unknown (none) — and exactly those must be sent. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: delete_important_date
tools.title: Delete an important date
tools.description: Permanently removes one important date. dateId and expectedUpdatedAt are the date's id and updatedAt from list_important_dates; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. That read requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: list_profile_facts
tools.title: List a person's profile facts
tools.description: Reads one section of a person's profile facts — contact-methods, addresses, work, pets, first-meeting, food-preferences, or tags — archived people included. Each record has the id and updatedAt its update and delete need, and the answer's personUpdatedAt is the expectedPersonUpdatedAt every fact write needs. Set includeOptions to "true" to also get the ids that section's writes may name (contact types and labels, organizations, pet categories); optionSearch filters them, and nextOptionsCursor goes back as optionCursor for more. Records page with nextCursor and cursor. A section the workspace hides returns nothing.

tools.name: add_contact_method
tools.title: Add a contact method
tools.description: Adds a contact method — an email address, phone number, website, social or messaging handle — to a person. typeId and labelIds come from list_profile_facts with section contact-methods and includeOptions "true"; isPrimary makes it the person's main one. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused. There is no retry key: repeating it adds a second record.

tools.name: update_contact_method
tools.title: Update a contact method
tools.description: Replaces one of a person's contact methods with the value sent; notes left out are cleared. factId is the record's id from list_profile_facts (section contact-methods). expectedUpdatedAt is the record's updatedAt from list_profile_facts. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: add_address
tools.title: Add an address
tools.description: Adds a postal address to a person; send at least one of street, city, region, postalCode, country, or displayName. labelIds come from list_profile_facts with section addresses and includeOptions "true"; isPrimary makes it the main address. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused. There is no retry key: repeating it adds a second record.

tools.name: update_address
tools.title: Update an address
tools.description: Replaces one of a person's addresses with the value sent; parts left out are cleared, and at least one must remain. factId is the record's id from list_profile_facts (section addresses). expectedUpdatedAt is the record's updatedAt from list_profile_facts. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: add_job
tools.title: Add a job
tools.description: Adds a job to a person's work history: a title, and optionally an organization (organizationId from list_profile_facts with section work and includeOptions "true", or organizationName), dates, and whether it is current. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused. There is no retry key: repeating it adds a second record.

tools.name: update_job
tools.title: Update a job
tools.description: Replaces one job in a person's work history with the value sent; optional fields left out are cleared. factId is the record's id from list_profile_facts (section work). expectedUpdatedAt is the record's updatedAt from list_profile_facts. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: add_pet
tools.title: Add a pet
tools.description: Adds a pet to a person: a name, a category (categoryId from list_profile_facts with section pets and includeOptions "true"), or both, and optional notes. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused. There is no retry key: repeating it adds a second record.

tools.name: update_pet
tools.title: Update a pet
tools.description: Replaces one of a person's pets with the value sent; fields left out are cleared, and a name or category must remain. factId is the record's id from list_profile_facts (section pets). expectedUpdatedAt is the record's updatedAt from list_profile_facts. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: add_first_meeting
tools.title: Record how you first met
tools.description: Records how a person was first met: where (placeText), notes, and who introduced you (introducedByPersonId, another person from list_people); send at least one. A person holds one first meeting, so when one exists this is refused as stale; change it with update_first_meeting. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: update_first_meeting
tools.title: Update how you first met
tools.description: Replaces a person's first meeting with the value sent; fields left out are cleared, and at least one must remain. The person holds one such record; expectedUpdatedAt is its updatedAt from list_profile_facts (section first-meeting). expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: add_food_preferences
tools.title: Record food preferences
tools.description: Records a person's food preferences as free text. A person holds one such record, so when one exists this is refused as stale; change it with update_food_preferences. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: update_food_preferences
tools.title: Update food preferences
tools.description: Replaces a person's food preferences text. The person holds one such record; expectedUpdatedAt is its updatedAt from list_profile_facts (section food-preferences). expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: update_person_tags
tools.title: Set a person's tags
tools.description: Replaces a person's whole set of tags with tagIds (from list_tags); an empty list removes every tag. To add or remove one tag across people without replacing the rest, use add_tag_to_people or remove_tag_from_people. The person holds one such record; expectedUpdatedAt is its updatedAt from list_profile_facts (section tags). expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: delete_profile_fact
tools.title: Delete a profile fact
tools.description: Permanently removes one profile-fact record — a contact method, address, job, or pet — or clears a person's first meeting or food preferences. factId and expectedUpdatedAt are the record's id and updatedAt from list_profile_facts in the same section; for first-meeting and food-preferences the id is the person's. Tags cannot be deleted here: clear them with update_person_tags and an empty list. expectedPersonUpdatedAt is personUpdatedAt from list_profile_facts or from the last profile-fact write on this person; every fact write changes it, so use the newest. A stale one is refused as a conflict. list_profile_facts requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people and sections the workspace hides are refused.

tools.name: list_life_events
tools.title: List a person's life events
tools.description: Lists up to 100 of a person's life events — a move, a new job, a wedding, a loss — archived people included, each with its id, updatedAt, name or type, note, and date with the precision it was stored with, and the workspace's life-event types with the ids record_life_event takes. A section the workspace hides returns no events.

tools.name: record_life_event
tools.title: Record a life event
tools.description: Records a life event on a person and returns it with its id: a name, a type (typeId from list_life_events), or both, an optional note, and a date. precision says which of year, month, and day the date has — full (all three), year_month, month_day, year, month, day, or unknown (none) — and exactly those must be sent. There is no retry key: repeating it records a second event. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: update_life_event
tools.title: Update a life event
tools.description: Replaces a life event with the value sent (fields left out are cleared). lifeEventId and expectedUpdatedAt are the event's id and updatedAt from list_life_events; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. That read requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. precision says which of year, month, and day the date has — full (all three), year_month, month_day, year, month, day, or unknown (none) — and exactly those must be sent. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: delete_life_event
tools.title: Delete a life event
tools.description: Permanently removes a life event. lifeEventId and expectedUpdatedAt are the event's id and updatedAt from list_life_events; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. That read requires people:profile:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: list_relationships
tools.title: List a person's relationships
tools.description: Lists one person's relationships in both directions (for example parent of, or child of), archived people included: each has its id, updatedAt, relationship type and labels, and the two people's ids with the related person's name. Pages with limit and nextCursor; a workspace that hides relationships returns none. Use the id and updatedAt with update_relationship and delete_relationship.

tools.name: list_relationship_types
tools.title: List relationship types
tools.description: Lists the workspace's relationship types with their ids and their forward and reverse labels (parent of / child of), for create_relationship and update_relationship. search filters by name, nextCursor pages, and selected (up to 20 ids) resolves types you already hold.

tools.name: create_relationship
tools.title: Relate two people
tools.description: Relates personId to targetPersonId with a relationship type (relationshipTypeId from list_relationship_types, which requires relationships:read). personId is the edge's from person, so the type's forward label reads from personId to targetPersonId and its reverse label back. Both people must be active. One edge supplies both directions, so never create the reverse as well. Safe to repeat: an edge that already exists is answered as existing rather than duplicated.

tools.name: update_relationship
tools.title: Change a relationship's type
tools.description: Changes only the relationship type of one edge (relationshipTypeId from list_relationship_types). relationshipId and expectedUpdatedAt are the edge's id and updatedAt from list_relationships for personId, either person of the edge; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. list_relationships requires relationships:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Both people must be active.

tools.name: delete_relationship
tools.title: Remove a relationship
tools.description: Permanently removes one relationship between two people, in both directions, without deleting either person. relationshipId and expectedUpdatedAt are the edge's id and updatedAt from list_relationships; a stale revision is refused as a conflict. list_relationships requires relationships:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. Both people must be active.

tools.name: list_activity_options
tools.title: List activity types and emotions
tools.description: Lists the workspace's activity types and emotions with their ids, for record_activity (activityTypeId, emotionIds) and record_call (emotionIds), and whether notes and activities may be recorded. Each list has its own search and cursor (activityTypeSearch and activityTypeCursor, emotionSearch and emotionCursor).

tools.name: list_conversation_options
tools.title: List conversation channels
tools.description: Lists the workspace's conversation channel types and emotions with their ids, and whether calls and conversations may be recorded. Read it before record_conversation, which needs a channelTypeId.

tools.name: record_note
tools.title: Record a note
tools.description: Adds a note to one person's profile and returns it with its id. isFavorited pins it to the Today page's favourite notes. Pass your own requestId (a UUID v4) and reuse it when you retry, so the retry returns the original record instead of adding a second one. Once that record is deleted, its requestId stays used: replaying the create is refused as a conflict (interaction_request_deleted) rather than recording it again. update_note and delete_note change it under interactions:write.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: record_activity
tools.title: Record an activity
tools.description: Records something done together with one or more people (participantIds from list_people): when it happened (an ISO instant with offset), a short summary, and optionally a description, an activity type, and emotions from list_activity_options. It counts as being in touch: when it happened after a person's last contact, their stay-in-touch cadence's last contact moves to it and its next due date follows. Pass your own requestId (a UUID v4) and reuse it when you retry, so the retry returns the original record instead of adding a second one. Once that record is deleted, its requestId stays used: replaying the create is refused as a conflict (interaction_request_deleted) rather than recording it again.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. tools.name: list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: Lists the workspace's tasks with their ids, status, due instant, linked person, and updatedAt, optionally only one person's (personId), one status (open, completed, or cancelled), or those due by dueBefore (an inclusive ISO instant). Pages with limit and nextCursor; a cursor is bound to its filters, so changing a filter starts again from the first page.

tools.name: get_task
tools.title: Get a task
tools.description: Reads one task, with its linked person if it has one. Its updatedAt is the expectedUpdatedAt update_task needs.

tools.name: create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Creates an open task with a title and optionally a description, a due instant (dueAt), and a linked person (personId from list_people), and returns it with its id and updatedAt. Pass your own requestId (a UUID v4) and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the original, and a changed payload under it is refused as a conflict. Once the task is deleted its requestId stays used: replaying the create is refused as a conflict (task_request_deleted) rather than recreating it.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. tools.name: update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: Changes a task's title, description, due instant, linked person, or status (open or cancelled; use set_task_completion to complete it). Send expectedUpdatedAt as the updatedAt from get_task or list_tasks: if the task changed since, the call is refused as a conflict, so read it again. get_task and list_tasks require tasks:read; a token without it cannot obtain a task's id or revision. tools.name: set_task_completion
tools.title: Complete or reopen a task
tools.description: Marks a task completed (completed: true) or reopens it (completed: false); taskId comes from list_tasks. get_task and list_tasks require tasks:read; a token without it cannot obtain a task's id or revision. Safe to repeat: setting the state it already has changes nothing.

tools.name: list_reminders
tools.title: List a person's reminders
tools.description: Lists one person's calendar reminders, each with its id, schedule, whether it is active, its next occurrence, and the updatedAt its changes need, and the person's stay-in-touch cadence if they have one (its id, interval, last contact, next due instant, and updatedAt). Pages reminders with limit and nextCursor.

tools.name: create_reminder
tools.title: Create a reminder
tools.description: Creates a calendar reminder about one person (personId from list_people) and schedules its occurrences: a title, the date it starts from (anchorOn), a local time of day to send it (sendTime, HH:MM), and how it repeats (recurrenceUnit none for once, or every recurrenceInterval days, weeks, months, or years). Pass your own requestId (a UUID v4) and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the original, and a changed payload under it is refused as a conflict. Once the reminder is deleted its requestId stays used: replaying the create is refused as a conflict (reminder_request_deleted) rather than recreating it. Archived people are read-only.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. tools.name: set_reminder_active
tools.title: Pause or resume a reminder
tools.description: Disables (active: false) or re-enables (active: true) a reminder; reminderId comes from list_reminders. list_reminders requires reminders:read; a token without it cannot obtain a reminder's or a cadence's id or revision. Disabling cancels its future occurrences that have not been attempted, for every member, and re-enabling schedules them again. Safe to repeat: setting the current state changes nothing.

tools.name: set_stay_in_touch_cadence
tools.title: Set a stay-in-touch cadence
tools.description: Sets how often to stay in touch with one person (every intervalCount days, weeks, months, or years). A person has one cadence: setting it again with a new requestId replaces it and restarts its due date. Recording a later activity, call, or conversation with the person moves its next due date on. Pass your own requestId (a UUID v4) and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the original, and a changed payload under it is refused as a conflict. After delete_stay_in_touch_cadence an earlier requestId creates the cadence again. Archived people are read-only.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.title: Delete a task
tools.description: Permanently deletes a task: get_task then answers not found, and it leaves list_tasks, Today, the attention queue, and search. Send expectedUpdatedAt as the task's updatedAt from get_task or list_tasks; a task changed since is refused as a conflict (task_stale), so read it again. get_task and list_tasks require tasks:read; a token without it cannot obtain a task's id or revision. The task's requestId stays used: replaying the create_task call that made it is refused as a conflict (task_request_deleted) rather than recreating it. Archived linked people are read-only.

tools.name: update_reminder
tools.title: Edit a reminder
tools.description: Edits a reminder's title, anchorOn, sendTime, recurrenceUnit, or recurrenceInterval, at least one of them; any member may edit any reminder about a workspace person. expectedUpdatedAt is the reminder's updatedAt from list_reminders (reminder_stale when it changed since). list_reminders requires reminders:read; a token without it cannot obtain a reminder's or a cadence's id or revision. Its unattempted future occurrences are replaced from the new schedule for every member who had them, each in their own time zone and channels; delivered and in-flight ones are kept, and a disabled reminder stays disabled. A reminder made from an important date is refused (reminder_managed_by_source): change the date with update_important_date instead. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: delete_reminder
tools.title: Delete a reminder
tools.description: Deletes a reminder about a person: its unattempted future occurrences stop as disabling stops them, delivered and in-flight ones are kept as evidence, and it leaves list_reminders and Today. expectedUpdatedAt is its updatedAt from list_reminders. A stale revision is refused as a conflict: read it again. list_reminders requires reminders:read; a token without it cannot obtain a reminder's or a cadence's id or revision. Its requestId stays used: replaying the create_reminder call that made it is refused as a conflict (reminder_request_deleted). A reminder made from an important date is refused (reminder_managed_by_source): change or delete the date instead. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: delete_stay_in_touch_cadence
tools.title: Remove a stay-in-touch cadence
tools.description: Removes a person's stay-in-touch cadence. cadenceId is its id from list_reminders or set_stay_in_touch_cadence (replacing a cadence keeps its id), and expectedUpdatedAt its updatedAt from list_reminders; recording an interaction moves it, so read just before. A stale revision is refused as a conflict: read it again. list_reminders requires reminders:read; a token without it cannot obtain a reminder's or a cadence's id or revision. Its due item leaves Today and the attention queue, and later interactions do not bring it back. Deleting also removes its request receipts, so replaying an earlier set_stay_in_touch_cadence requestId creates the cadence again. Archived people are read-only.

tools.name: list_journal_items
tools.title: List the journal
tools.description: Lists the workspace's journal timeline, newest first: posts with their bodies, day ratings, and activities put on the journal with their summaries and participants, each with its journal item id. It also lists recent activities that are not on the journal yet, for add_activity_to_journal. Pages with limit and nextCursor. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

tools.name: get_journal_item
tools.title: Get a journal item
tools.description: Reads one journal item by its id from list_journal_items: a post with its body and updatedAt, a day rating, or an activity on the journal with its summary and participants. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

tools.name: create_journal_post
tools.title: Write a journal post
tools.description: Writes a journal post — a body, the instant it is about (occurredAt), and an optional title — and returns it with its id, which is also its journal item id. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it. Pass your own requestId and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and post return the post it created, and a changed body, title, or occurredAt under it is refused as a conflict. Once delete_journal_item removes the post, its requestId stays used: replaying the create is refused as a conflict (journal_request_deleted) rather than writing it again.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: update_journal_post
tools.title: Update a journal post
tools.description: Replaces a post's body, occurredAt, and title with the values sent; a title left out is cleared. itemId is the post's id from create_journal_post or list_journal_items. Send expectedUpdatedAt as the post's updatedAt from get_journal_item or list_journal_items to refuse a concurrent edit as a conflict; left out, the post is overwritten unchecked, losing any edit made since you read it. list_journal_items and get_journal_item require journal:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Optional revision check: the post's updatedAt exactly as a read returned it. When it is no longer the post's revision the edit is refused (409) and nothing changes.

tools.name: set_day_rating
tools.title: Rate a day
tools.description: Rates a calendar day (ratedOn) from 1 to 5, with an optional comment. The workspace keeps one rating per date, shared by every member: rating a rated date replaces its rating, and a comment left out is cleared. Safe to repeat. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

tools.name: add_activity_to_journal
tools.title: Put an activity on the journal
tools.description: Puts an existing activity (activityId from record_activity, or from the activities list_journal_items offers, which requires journal:read) on the journal timeline and returns its journal item id. An activity already on the journal, or outside the workspace, is refused as not found. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

tools.name: delete_journal_item
tools.title: Delete a journal item
tools.description: Permanently deletes one journal item by its id from list_journal_items: a post or a day rating is deleted, while for an activity only its place on the journal is removed and the activity itself stays. A deleted post's requestId stays used: replaying the create_journal_post call that made it is refused as a conflict (journal_request_deleted). There is no revision check. list_journal_items and get_journal_item require journal:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. The journal is workspace-wide, not private to its author: every member can read, edit, and delete it.

tools.name: list_gifts_and_debts
tools.title: List a person's gifts and debts
tools.description: Lists one person's gifts, debts, and recurring debts with their ids, statuses, and amounts (decimal strings with a three-letter currency code), and the default and supported currencies for new ones. Gifts and debts page independently: pass nextGiftCursor back as giftCursor and nextDebtCursor as debtCursor. An archived person's records stay readable.

tools.name: list_debt_settlements
tools.title: List a debt's settlements
tools.description: Lists one debt's settlement history, newest first: when it was settled, the optional reason, and the optional settlement photo's file id and name with whether it is still available. debtId comes from list_gifts_and_debts; pages with limit and nextCursor.

tools.name: create_gift
tools.title: Record a gift
tools.description: Records a gift on a person's profile — an idea, a plan, or one given or received — and returns it with its id. amount is a decimal string (for example "12.50") and currencyCode a three-letter code the workspace supports, listed by list_gifts_and_debts. The amount is optional. recipientPersonId optionally names another person of the workspace who receives it; attachmentFileId optionally names an available file of the workspace that is not an avatar, from list_files (files:read). Pass your own requestId and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the gift the first call wrote, a different payload or person under it is refused as a conflict (gift_request_conflict), and once that gift was deleted it is refused (gift_request_deleted) rather than recorded again. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: set_gift_status
tools.title: Change a gift's status
tools.description: Moves a gift along its statuses: an idea may become planned, given, or received; a planned gift may be given or received; any gift may be archived, and archived is final — it cannot be moved again. A move that is not allowed is refused as a conflict; asking for the status it already has answers unchanged. Send expectedUpdatedAt, the gift's updatedAt, to refuse the change as a conflict (gift_stale) when it changed since; left out, the change applies to whatever the gift is now. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: create_debt
tools.title: Record a debt
tools.description: Records money the person owes you (direction they_owe) or you owe them (i_owe), with a status, an optional reason, and returns it with its id. amount is a decimal string (for example "12.50") and currencyCode a three-letter code the workspace supports, listed by list_gifts_and_debts. A settlement may carry a reason and settlementPhotoFileId, the id of an available JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of the same person. Pass your own requestId and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the debt the first call wrote, a different payload or person under it is refused as a conflict (gift_request_conflict), and once that debt was deleted it is refused (gift_request_deleted) rather than recorded again. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: set_debt_status
tools.title: Settle, reopen, or cancel a debt
tools.description: Moves a debt between open, settled, and cancelled: an open debt may be settled or cancelled, a settled debt may reopen, and cancelled is final. Settling adds an entry to the debt's permanent settlement history. A settlement may carry a reason and settlementPhotoFileId, the id of an available JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of the same person. Asking for the status it already has answers unchanged. Send expectedUpdatedAt, the debt's updatedAt, to refuse the change as a conflict (gift_stale) when it changed since; left out, the change applies to whatever the debt is now. A refused move records no settlement. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: delete_debt
tools.title: Delete a debt
tools.description: Permanently deletes one debt together with its whole settlement history; nothing can restore it. A debt a recurring debt charged leaves the recurring rule and its other charges in place. There is no revision check. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: create_recurring_debt
tools.title: Create a recurring debt
tools.description: Creates a rule that charges the person the same debt every intervalMonths months on dayOfMonth, from startsOn until the optional endsOn. Every period already due is charged at once, one open debt per period. amount is a decimal string (for example "12.50") and currencyCode a three-letter code the workspace supports, listed by list_gifts_and_debts. Pass your own requestId and reuse it when you retry: the same requestId and payload return the rule the first call wrote, a different payload or person under it is refused as a conflict (gift_request_conflict), and once that rule was deleted it is refused (gift_request_deleted) rather than recorded again. A replay charges nothing again. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

requestId.description: Retry key, a UUID v4 you generate. Pass your own and reuse the same value when you retry this exact call, so a retry returns the original record instead of creating a second one; a changed payload under the same key is refused as a conflict. Left out, the server mints one and the call cannot be safely retried.

tools.name: update_recurring_debt
tools.title: Update, pause, or resume a recurring debt
tools.description: Changes a recurring debt's terms, or pauses (active false) or resumes (active true) it. A period already charged is never charged again, resuming skips the periods that passed while paused, and a change that leaves due periods uncharged charges them at once. Send null to clear endsOn or reason, and change at least one field besides expectedUpdatedAt. Send expectedUpdatedAt, the rule's updatedAt, to refuse the change as a conflict (gift_stale) when it changed since; left out, the change applies to whatever the rule is now. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: delete_recurring_debt
tools.title: Delete a recurring debt
tools.description: Permanently deletes a recurring debt so it charges nothing more. The debts it already charged stay, each to be settled or cancelled on its own. There is no revision check. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: update_gift
tools.title: Edit a gift
tools.description: Edits a gift's name, amount with currencyCode (sent together), eventAt, comment, url, recipientPersonId, or attachmentFileId; set_gift_status moves its status. A field left out keeps its value and null clears an optional one; name cannot be cleared, and at least one field is required. amount is a decimal string (for example "12.50") and currencyCode a three-letter code the workspace supports, listed by list_gifts_and_debts. An attachment replaces the gift's attachment and null removes it; the previous file stays in the person's files. expectedUpdatedAt is required, and a gift changed since is refused as a conflict (gift_stale). Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. Any member may edit any gift. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: delete_gift
tools.title: Delete a gift
tools.description: Permanently deletes one gift; nothing restores it, and replaying the create_gift call that made it is refused as a conflict (gift_request_deleted). expectedUpdatedAt is required, and a gift changed since is refused as a conflict (gift_stale). An attached file is not deleted: only its link to the gift goes, and the file stays in the person's files. To keep a gift out of the way instead, archive it with set_gift_status. Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: update_debt
tools.title: Edit a debt
tools.description: Edits a debt's amount, currencyCode, direction, or reason; set_debt_status moves its status. A field left out keeps its value, reason null clears it, and at least one field is required. amount is a decimal string (for example "12.50") and currencyCode a three-letter code the workspace supports, listed by list_gifts_and_debts. Amount, currency, and direction change only while the debt is open and has never been settled: once settled, even if reopened, they are refused (debt_values_locked) while its reason stays editable, and a cancelled debt refuses every edit. Editing a recurring charge changes neither its rule nor the other charges. expectedUpdatedAt is required, and a debt changed since is refused as a conflict (gift_stale). Ids and updatedAt come from list_gifts_and_debts or the last write; list_gifts_and_debts requires gifts:read, and a token without it cannot obtain them. An archived person's gifts and debts are read-only.

tools.name: list_files
tools.title: List a person's files
tools.description: Lists one person's photos and then documents with their fileId, filename, title, kind, mimeType, byteSize, and availability (available, missing, processing, or quarantined); the avatar image and removed files are never listed. It returns no file bytes: uploading and downloading are REST routes, not tools. A file id names a gift's attachmentFileId or a settlement's settlementPhotoFileId. Pages with limit and nextCursor.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.title: Delete a person's file
tools.description: Permanently deletes one of the person's documents or photos: its stored bytes and its link to the person are deleted, so it is no longer listed or downloadable, and no tool can restore it. A gift that attached it keeps its attachmentFileId, now naming a removed file, and a debt settlement whose photo it was reports that photo as unavailable. fileId comes from list_files, which requires files:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. There is no revision check; a file still being processed is refused as a conflict, and an avatar, another person's file, or an archived person's file is not found.

tools.name: list_vocabulary_entries
tools.title: List a vocabulary
tools.description: Lists one vocabulary section's entries with their ids, names or labels, order, active and default flags, updatedAt, how many records use each (referenceCount), and capabilities saying what each entry allows; the section's capabilities say whether it takes new entries. Sections: tags, contact-labels, contact-method-types, activity-types, life-event-types, gender-options, relationship-types, reminder-rules, profile-modules, and the fixed emotion-options and pet-categories. Vocabularies are administrative: the token's member must currently be an owner or admin of the workspace, or the call is refused as forbidden.

tools.name: create_tag
tools.title: Create a tag
tools.description: Creates a workspace tag to put on people with add_tag_to_people or update_person_tags. Returns the new entry with its id. There is no retry key. A name already used in the section is refused as a conflict. Vocabularies are administrative: the token's member must currently be an owner or admin of the workspace, or the call is refused as forbidden.

tools.name: update_tag

Change at least one field. Vocabularies are administrative: the token's member must currently be an owner or admin of the workspace, or the call is refused as forbidden.

tools.description: Permanently deletes one entry; id and expectedUpdatedAt are its id and updatedAt from list_vocabulary_entries, which requires vocabularies:read; a token without it cannot obtain one. While records still use the entry the call is refused as replacement required, and succeeds only with replacementId, another entry of the same section, to which those records move. Required and seeded entries, emotions, and pet categories cannot be deleted. Vocabularies are administrative: the token's member must currently be an owner or admin of the workspace, or the call is refused as forbidden.
